nodes.Fetch Staging Data:
SELECT 
    n.run_id,
    n.ta_households_current,
    n.ta_households_prev_year,
    n.ta_yoy_pct,
    n.rough_sleeping_current,
    n.rough_sleeping_prev_year,
    n.bb_spend_total_000,
    n.nightly_paid_spend_total_000,
    n.hb_sa_caseload_total,
    n.housing_register_total,
    (SELECT json_agg(s ORDER BY s.lad24cd)
     FROM staging_la_signals s
     WHERE s.run_id = n.run_id) AS la_signals,
    (SELECT json_agg(c ORDER BY c.section3_rank)
     FROM staging_convergence c
     WHERE c.run_id = n.run_id) AS convergence,
    (SELECT json_agg(t ORDER BY t.tenant_type, t.rank_position)
     FROM staging_tenant_type_rankings t
     WHERE t.run_id = n.run_id) AS tenant_rankings
FROM staging_national n
WHERE n.run_id = (SELECT MAX(run_id) FROM staging_runs WHERE status = 'complete');
nodes.Define Sections:
const data = $('Fetch Staging Data').first().json;
const run_id = data.run_id;

const national = {
  ta_current: data.ta_households_current,
  ta_prev: data.ta_households_prev_year,
  ta_yoy_pct: data.ta_yoy_pct,
  rough_sleeping_current: data.rough_sleeping_current,
  rough_sleeping_prev: data.rough_sleeping_prev_year,
  bb_spend: data.bb_spend_total_000,
  nightly_spend: data.nightly_paid_spend_total_000,
  hb_sa_total: data.hb_sa_caseload_total,
  housing_register: data.housing_register_total
};

const convergence = data.convergence;
const la_signals = data.la_signals;
const tenant_rankings = data.tenant_rankings;

const byType = {};
for (const row of tenant_rankings) {
  if (!byType[row.tenant_type]) byType[row.tenant_type] = [];
  byType[row.tenant_type].push(row);
}

const sections = [
  {
    section_id: 'section_2',
    title: 'Market Context',
    data: national,
    generation_prompt: `You are writing Section 2 (Market Context) of a confidential exempt accommodation market intelligence report for an experienced property investment professional. Write in McKinsey/BCG style — conclusion first, evidence second, no padding. 

DATA:
${JSON.stringify(national, null, 2)}

REQUIREMENTS:
- Open with the single most important national headline
- Cover TA trend (current vs prior year, YoY%), rough sleeping, B&B spend, nightly paid spend, HB SA caseload, housing register
- All figures must be stated explicitly — do not approximate
- Flag any data quality issues if signals are missing or zero
- 300-400 words
- No bullet points — flowing prose with subheadings
- All spend figures are stored in £thousands. Multiply by 1,000 before stating them. So bb_spend: 664821.57 = £664.8 million, not £664,821.
- Output HTML only, no markdown, no preamble`,
    assessor_criteria: `Assess this Section 2 draft against these criteria. Respond with JSON only: {"pass": true/false, "issues": ["issue1", "issue2"]}

CRITERIA:
1. Opens with a clear conclusion, not a scene-setter
2. All data figures stated explicitly and match the source data provided
3. No hallucinated figures or unsupported claims
4. 300-400 words
5. McKinsey/BCG tone — direct, no padding
6. Valid HTML output`
  },
  {
    section_id: 'section_3',
    title: 'View One — By Local Authority',
    data: { convergence: convergence.slice(0, 20), la_signals: la_signals.slice(0, 30) },
    generation_prompt: `You are writing Section 3 (View One — By Local Authority) of a confidential exempt accommodation market intelligence report. This section identifies the top 3 LAs for multi-tenant exempt accommodation investment using a UCWS lens (resettlement cohort, HMO-basis, room-by-room HB, SAR as rate floor) and HSS lens (complex needs, personal care, CQC registered).

DATA — All LAs ranked by convergence breadth (how many tenant type top-3 lists they appear in):
${JSON.stringify(convergence.slice(0, 20), null, 2)}

FULL LA SIGNAL DATA:
${JSON.stringify(la_signals.slice(0, 30), null, 2)}

REQUIREMENTS:
- Apply viability filters before selecting your top 3: You MUST NOT select any of the following LAs under any circumstances, regardless of their demand signals: City of London, Westminster, Camden, Islington, Hackney, Tower Hamlets, Southwark, Lambeth, Wandsworth, Hammersmith and Fulham, Kensington and Chelsea, and all other inner London boroughs. These are excluded on yield grounds and this exclusion is non-negotiable., exclude LAs with submission gaps (ta_current = 0 or data_quality flags)
- Select the 3 most viable LAs and state your selection rationale explicitly
- For each LA: profile the demand signals, note the tenant type convergence, flag EFS/S114 status, note data quality issues
- Assess each LA through both UCWS and HSS lenses separately
- Do not score or rank within your top 3 — present as equally viable options with different profiles
- 600-800 words total
- Output HTML only`,
    assessor_criteria: `Assess this Section 3 draft. Respond with JSON only: {"pass": true/false, "issues": ["issue1", "issue2"]}

CRITERIA:
1. Exactly 3 LAs profiled
2. Viability filter explicitly applied and rationale stated — inner London exclusions or similar must be explained
3. Both UCWS and HSS lenses applied to each LA separately
4. All figures match source data — no hallucinated numbers
5. EFS/S114 flags correctly reported
6. Data quality issues flagged where present
7. No composite scores or rankings within the 3
8. 600-800 words
9. Valid HTML`
  },
  {
    section_id: 'section_4_single_homeless',
    title: 'View Two — Single Homeless Adults',
    data: { rankings: byType['single_homeless']?.slice(0, 10) },
    generation_prompt: `You are writing the Single Homeless Adults subsection of Section 4 (View Two — By Tenant Type) of a confidential exempt accommodation market intelligence report.

TENANT TYPE CONTEXT:
Single homeless adults placed in TA by LAs under the Housing Act 1996 (as amended). Primary UCWS cohort — no personal care, HMO-basis, room-by-room HB at SAR. Signal: households_in_ta from MHCLG statutory homelessness Q2 2025.

TOP 10 LAs BY TA HOUSEHOLDS (single homeless signal):
${JSON.stringify(byType['single_homeless']?.slice(0, 10), null, 2)}

REQUIREMENTS:
- Identify the top 3 viable LAs for single homeless exempt accommodation
- Apply viability filter — exclude inner London where yield economics don't work
- For each: state the TA volume, trend, and why this LA presents opportunity
- UCWS lens only for this cohort — no personal care element
- Note where this overlaps with Section 3 LA selections (convergence signal)
- 300-400 words
- Output HTML only`,
    assessor_criteria: `Assess this Single Homeless subsection. Respond with JSON only: {"pass": true/false, "issues": ["issue1", "issue2"]}

CRITERIA:
1. Exactly 3 LAs identified with viability rationale
2. Figures match source data
3. UCWS lens applied correctly — no personal care references
4. Convergence with Section 3 noted where applicable
5. 300-400 words
6. Valid HTML`
  },
  {
    section_id: 'section_4_rough_sleepers',
    title: 'View Two — Rough Sleepers',
    data: { rankings: byType['rough_sleepers']?.slice(0, 10) },
    generation_prompt: `You are writing the Rough Sleepers subsection of Section 4 of a confidential exempt accommodation market intelligence report.

TENANT TYPE CONTEXT:
Rough sleepers — individuals counted in the annual MHCLG snapshot. Primary UCWS cohort with high support needs. Often accompanied by substance misuse, mental health, and offending history. Signal: rough_sleeping_current from 2025 snapshot.

TOP 10 LAs BY ROUGH SLEEPING COUNT:
${JSON.stringify(byType['rough_sleepers']?.slice(0, 10), null, 2)}

REQUIREMENTS:
- Identify top 3 viable LAs
- Apply viability filter
- Note the snapshot nature of the data — single night count, may understate true prevalence
- UCWS lens — these are high-need single adults, room-by-room HB at SAR
- 300-400 words
- Output HTML only`,
    assessor_criteria: `Assess this Rough Sleepers subsection. Respond with JSON only: {"pass": true/false, "issues": ["issue1", "issue2"]}

CRITERIA:
1. Exactly 3 LAs with viability rationale
2. Figures match source data
3. Data limitation of single-night snapshot noted
4. UCWS lens applied correctly
5. 300-400 words
6. Valid HTML`
  },
  {
    section_id: 'section_4_care_leavers',
    title: 'View Two — Care Leavers',
    data: { rankings: byType['care_leavers']?.slice(0, 10) },
    generation_prompt: `You are writing the Care Leavers subsection of Section 4 of a confidential exempt accommodation market intelligence report.

TENANT TYPE CONTEXT:
Care leavers aged 17-21 in semi-independent accommodation. LA has a statutory duty to commission appropriate accommodation. Primary UCWS cohort — Ofsted-registered supported accommodation from 2024 onwards. Signal: semi_independent placements from DfE 2024 data.

TOP 10 LAs BY SEMI-INDEPENDENT PLACEMENTS:
${JSON.stringify(byType['care_leavers']?.slice(0, 10), null, 2)}

REQUIREMENTS:
- Identify top 3 viable LAs
- Note the Ofsted registration requirement introduced in 2024 — this raises the bar for providers but creates a quality signal for commissioners
- Both UCWS (younger, lower complexity) and HSS (complex needs care leavers) lens applicable
- 300-400 words
- Output HTML only`,
    assessor_criteria: `Assess this Care Leavers subsection. Respond with JSON only: {"pass": true/false, "issues": ["issue1", "issue2"]}

CRITERIA:
1. Exactly 3 LAs with viability rationale
2. Figures match source data
3. Ofsted registration requirement noted
4. Both UCWS and HSS lenses applied
5. 300-400 words
6. Valid HTML`
  },
  {
    section_id: 'section_4_domestic_abuse',
    title: 'View Two — Domestic Abuse Survivors',
    data: { rankings: byType['domestic_abuse']?.slice(0, 10) },
    generation_prompt: `You are writing the Domestic Abuse Survivors subsection of Section 4 of a confidential exempt accommodation market intelligence report.

TENANT TYPE CONTEXT:
Domestic abuse survivors referred through MARAC (Multi-Agency Risk Assessment Conference). Signal is cases per 10,000 adult females — a rate not a volume, so smaller LAs with high rates are surfaced alongside large urban areas. Data is PFA-level (police force area) mapped to LA via population weighting — all 32 London boroughs share Metropolitan Police figures.

TOP 10 LAs BY MARAC RATE PER 10K ADULT FEMALES:
${JSON.stringify(byType['domestic_abuse']?.slice(0, 10), null, 2)}

REQUIREMENTS:
- Identify top 3 viable LAs
- Explicitly note the PFA-to-LA mapping limitation — London boroughs share a single Met Police figure
- Note this is a rate signal not a volume signal — interpret accordingly
- UCWS lens primarily (move-on accommodation) with HSS element for complex cases
- Medium confidence rating — note data limitation
- 300-400 words
- Output HTML only`,
    assessor_criteria: `Assess this Domestic Abuse subsection. Respond with JSON only: {"pass": true/false, "issues": ["issue1", "issue2"]}

CRITERIA:
1. Exactly 3 LAs with viability rationale
2. PFA-to-LA mapping limitation explicitly stated
3. Rate vs volume distinction noted
4. Medium confidence flagged
5. 300-400 words
6. Valid HTML`
  },
  {
    section_id: 'section_4_older_complex',
    title: 'View Two — Older People / Complex Needs',
    data: { rankings: byType['older_complex']?.slice(0, 10) },
    generation_prompt: `You are writing the Older People / Complex Needs subsection of Section 4 of a confidential exempt accommodation market intelligence report.

TENANT TYPE CONTEXT:
Older people and adults with complex needs using Housing Benefit Supported Accommodation (HB SA). Signal is HB SA caseload — the broadest supported accommodation signal available at LA level from DWP Stat-Xplore. This cohort includes both UCWS-eligible (lower complexity, no personal care) and HSS-eligible (personal care, CQC registered provision) placements.

TOP 10 LAs BY HB SA CASELOAD:
${JSON.stringify(byType['older_complex']?.slice(0, 10), null, 2)}

REQUIREMENTS:
- Identify top 3 viable LAs
- Note that HB SA is a broad signal — it captures all supported accommodation types, not just older people/complex needs
- Explicitly separate UCWS opportunity (lower complexity residents, no personal care) from HSS opportunity (personal care, CQC registered)
- Medium confidence — signal breadth noted
- 300-400 words
- Output HTML only`,
    assessor_criteria: `Assess this Older Complex subsection. Respond with JSON only: {"pass": true/false, "issues": ["issue1", "issue2"]}

CRITERIA:
1. Exactly 3 LAs with viability rationale
2. HB SA signal breadth limitation noted
3. UCWS and HSS opportunities separated explicitly
4. Medium confidence flagged
5. 300-400 words
6. Valid HTML`
  },
  {
    section_id: 'section_5',
    title: 'Convergence Analysis',
    data: { convergence: convergence.slice(0, 20) },
    generation_prompt: `You are writing Section 5 (Convergence Analysis) of a confidential exempt accommodation market intelligence report. This section identifies where the LA view (Section 3) and the tenant type views (Section 4) agree — the highest conviction opportunities.

CONVERGENCE DATA (top 20 LAs by convergence breadth):
${JSON.stringify(convergence.slice(0, 20), null, 2)}

REQUIREMENTS:
- Identify LAs that appear in both Section 3 shortlist AND multiple Section 4 tenant type shortlists
- These are the highest conviction markets — demand confirmed across multiple independent signals
- Note where convergence is strong (3+ signals) vs moderate (2 signals)
- Note where Section 3 and Section 4 diverge — what that means analytically
- Do not re-profile the LAs — cross-reference only
- 300-400 words
- Output HTML only`,
    assessor_criteria: `Assess this Section 5 draft. Respond with JSON only: {"pass": true/false, "issues": ["issue1", "issue2"]}

CRITERIA:
1. Correctly identifies convergence between Section 3 and Section 4 selections
2. Distinguishes strong vs moderate convergence
3. Notes divergence where present and explains analytically
4. Does not re-profile LAs already covered in Sections 3 and 4
5. 300-400 words
6. Valid HTML`
  },
  {
    section_id: 'section_6',
    title: 'Risk Framework',
    data: national,
    generation_prompt: `You are writing Section 6 (Risk Framework) of a confidential exempt accommodation market intelligence report. This section covers sector-level external risks — not LA-specific risks.

CONTEXT:
- Exempt accommodation is unregistered supported housing — providers are not CQC registered unless delivering personal care
- Regulatory environment: MHCLG has consulted on registration requirements for exempt accommodation providers — outcome pending
- LHA rates: frozen or suppressed in many areas — SAR is the effective floor for single adults
- LA financial stress: EFS recipients and S114 notices indicate commissioning risk in some markets
- Demand trajectory: TA households nationally at ${national.ta_current} (Q2 2025), up ${national.ta_yoy_pct}% year-on-year

REQUIREMENTS:
- Cover: regulatory risk, LHA/rent viability risk, LA commissioning risk, market saturation risk, data confidence risk
- Each risk: state it, rate it (High/Medium/Low), note the mitigant
- Do not mention specific LAs — this is sector-level only
- 400-500 words
- Output HTML only`,
    assessor_criteria: `Assess this Section 6 draft. Respond with JSON only: {"pass": true/false, "issues": ["issue1", "issue2"]}

CRITERIA:
1. Covers all 5 risk categories: regulatory, LHA/rent, LA commissioning, market saturation, data confidence
2. Each risk rated and mitigant stated
3. No specific LAs mentioned
4. 400-500 words
5. Valid HTML`
  },
  {
    section_id: 'section_7',
    title: 'Data Appendix',
    data: { national, run_id },
    generation_prompt: `You are writing Section 7 (Data Appendix) of a confidential exempt accommodation market intelligence report. This section is factual and automated — no analysis.

REQUIREMENTS:
Generate an HTML table with the following data sources used in this report:

| Source | Publisher | Data Period | Geography | Key Limitations |
|--------|-----------|-------------|-----------|-----------------|
| Statutory Homelessness TA Live Tables | MHCLG | Q2 2025 (Jul-Sep) | LA | Suppression for small LAs |
| Revenue Outturn RO4 | MHCLG | 2024-25 | LA | Outturn not budget |
| ONS Mid-Year Population Estimates | ONS | 2024 | LA | 1-year lag |
| Census 2021 TS054 Tenure | ONS | 2021 | LA | Pre-cost-of-living |
| DfE Care Leaver Accommodation | DfE | 2024 | LA | Ofsted registration from 2024 changes comparability |
| IMD 2025 | MHCLG | 2025 | LA | LSOA-level aggregated to LA |
| HB SA Caseload | DWP Stat-Xplore | Latest month | LA | Broad signal — all supported accommodation types |
| Rough Sleeping Snapshot | MHCLG | 2025 | LA | Single-night count |
| LA Financial Stress (EFS + S114) | MHCLG/IfG | 2024-25 | LA | S114 incomplete pre-2018 |
| LAHS Social Housing Waiting Lists | MHCLG | Latest year | LA | Joint registers obscure true count |
| MARAC | SafeLives | 2024-25 | PFA | PFA not LA — population-weighted mapping applied |

Also include a methodology note covering: multi-dimensional ranking approach, no composite scores, PFA-to-LA mapping method, £350/week LHA proxy and its limitations.

Output HTML only — table and methodology note.`,
    assessor_criteria: `Assess this Section 7 draft. Respond with JSON only: {"pass": true/false, "issues": ["issue1", "issue2"]}

CRITERIA:
1. All 11 data sources present in the table
2. Methodology note covers all 4 required topics
3. Valid HTML table formatting
4. No analysis — factual only`
  },
  {
    section_id: 'section_1',
    title: 'Executive Summary',
    data: { national, convergence: convergence.slice(0, 5) },
    generation_prompt: `You are writing Section 1 (Executive Summary) of a confidential exempt accommodation market intelligence report. This is written last — it synthesises the conclusions from all other sections into a 250-300 word briefing for a C-suite reader.

NATIONAL CONTEXT:
${JSON.stringify(national, null, 2)}

TOP 5 LAs BY CONVERGENCE:
${JSON.stringify(convergence.slice(0, 5), null, 2)}

REQUIREMENTS:
- Lead with the single most important conclusion for an investor considering exempt accommodation
- Cover: national demand trajectory, top LA opportunities (reference Section 3 selections), strongest tenant type signals (reference Section 4), convergence conclusion (reference Section 5)
- Flag the key risk (reference Section 6)
- 250-300 words — tight, no padding
- McKinsey/BCG style — conclusion first throughout
- Output HTML only`,
    assessor_criteria: `Assess this Section 1 draft. Respond with JSON only: {"pass": true/false, "issues": ["issue1", "issue2"]}

CRITERIA:
1. Opens with a clear investment conclusion — not a scene-setter
2. References Section 3, 4, 5, and 6 conclusions correctly
3. 250-300 words
4. No new information not covered elsewhere in the report
5. Valid HTML`
  }
];

return sections.map(s => ({ json: s }));
